clue.text: All-the-way cost of travel?

parts.note: the clue reads like the price of a complete trip, punning on a public road whose name splits into words for complete and for ticket price

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: split the main road's name and it becomes a complete or all-the-way charge for a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A main public road can be read as two words meaning a full or utter ticket price.

clue.text: Shakespeare thought this stuff very florid.

definitions.text: Shakespeare thought this stuff very florid

parts.words: Shakespeare thought this stuff very florid
parts.note: in Love's Labour's Lost Berowne forswears phrases made of this crisp silk fabric, Shakespeare's image for over-ornate language

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' means cloth here, not things in general; the reference is Berowne's line about silken, over-dressed phrases.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp lustrous silk fabric, used in Love's Labour's Lost as a figure for affected, showy speech.

clue.text: A thousand quit the country dance.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'A thousand quit the country dance.', has no letter count and no definition: MORRIS less M (a thousand) gives the letters, but nothing defines the answer, so the clue looks cut short.
annotationWithheld.clue: A thousand quit the country dance.

clue.text: Expenditure 'for departures ?

definitions.meaning: money spent, the costs paid out of a budget
acts of leaving, of going away from a place

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether spending money counts as a way of leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending paid out of an account, and also acts of leaving, are both described by this plural noun.

clue.text: Fourteen pounds lost from the bag.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Fourteen pounds lost from the bag.', has no letter count and no definition: GLADSTONE less STONE (fourteen pounds) gives the letters, but nothing defines the answer, so the clue looks cut short.
annotationWithheld.clue: Fourteen pounds lost from the bag.

clue.text: Imperial activity, with pyrotechnic paniment?-

parts.note: the emperor Nero is said to have played the violin while Rome burned: music by an emperor with flames for its accompaniment

explanation.walkthrough: The print's 'paniment' is plainly 'accompaniment' with its start lost. 'Pyrotechnic' points to the great fire of Rome in AD 64.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing the violin, the pastime legend gives Nero during the burning of Rome.

clue.text: It sounds as if he might regret all the

annotationWithheld.clue: It sounds as if he might regret all the

clue.text: How a blessing is conveyed before the 9 o'clock news?

definitions.text: How a blessing is conveyed before the 9 o'clock news

parts.words: How a blessing is conveyed before the 9 o'clock news
parts.note: the big bell at Westminster chimed on BBC radio before the nine o'clock news; split into three words, the word for a blessing announces that bell being on air

explanation.walkthrough: Big Ben is the bell of the Westminster clock tower, whose chimes the BBC broadcast before its evening news bulletin.
explanation.definitionFit: An old literary word for a blessing or benediction.

clue.text: But this civic dignitary is, not necessarily birch-minded.

definitions.text: But this civic dignitary is, not necessarily birch-minded

parts.words: But this civic dignitary is, not necessarily birch-minded
parts.note: his title begins with the name of a tree of the birch family, yet that is no sign that he favours flogging with a birch

explanation.walkthrough: A birch was a cane for corporal punishment, so 'birch-minded' suggests a flogger; the tree in the title belongs to the birch family only botanically.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior member of a town or borough council in Britain, ranking just below the mayor.

clue.text: No go-between in the case of the workman.

definitions.text: No go-between in the case of the workman

parts.words: No go-between in the case of the workman
parts.note: direct, with no intermediary; and a workman is a hand, so the leading one is the top hand

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' as a word for a worker supplies the second reading; the phrase normally means direct, from the source.
explanation.definitionFit: Direct, gained personally rather than through someone else in between.

clue.text: Is this'what he did to his'victim? likely.

definitions.text: Is this'what he did to his'victim? likely

parts.words: Is this'what he did to his'victim? likely
parts.note: a criminal who attacks someone has fallen upon them, and the past tense of fall plus 'on' sounds like the word for such a lawbreaker

explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophes are print marks. The wordplay is a pun: a lawbreaker 'fell on' his victim.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has committed a serious crime.

clue.text: Not back to Sue ?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Not back to Sue ? (6)', gives NOT + SUE read backwards for the letters but has no definition of the London station, so it looks cut short.

clue.text: "Nor all that-gold " (Gray).

parts.note: Gray's Ode on the Death of a Favourite Cat ends 'Nor all that ___, gold': the missing word means shines or sparkles

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from Thomas Gray, echoing the proverb about gold and glitter; the dash marks the missing word.
explanation.definitionFit: An old form meaning sparkles or shines, used by Gray in his cat ode.

clue.text: Sounds an inclusive invitation from press.

indicators.note: Sounds tells us the phrase meant is heard spoken rather than written, a homophone signal

parts.note: calling everyone to come and eat, 'all dine', invites the whole company

explanation.surface: A newspaper seems to be sending an invitation that includes everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like newspapers but means a printing house: the Venetian press of Aldus Manutius.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes books printed by Aldus Manutius's Renaissance Venetian printing house, so coming from that publisher.

clue.text: Keats listened apparently in deep purple:

definitions.text: Keats listened apparently in deep purple

parts.words: Keats listened apparently in deep purple
parts.note: in Ode to a Nightingale Keats listens in the dark using an old poetic adverb; deep purple also suggests dark heather, which is called ling

explanation.walkthrough: Ling is a common name for heather, whose flowers are purple, so 'deep purple' can be read as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An old poetic word meaning in the dark, from Keats's line about hearing the nightingale.

clue.text: Maid in an old vessel.

indicators.note: old suggests something worn and reshaped by time, read here as a signal to rearrange the words before it

explanation.surface: A young woman is aboard an ancient ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' rearranges MAIDINAN and also describes the ship, a merchant vessel of the East India trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A large merchant ship of the East India Company trade, a kind of sailing craft.

clue.text: Where little Shirley Temple found animal crackers. :

definitions.text: Where little Shirley Temple found animal crackers

parts.words: Where little Shirley Temple found animal crackers
parts.note: Shirley Temple sang 'Animal Crackers in My Soup'; the phrase also means in serious trouble

explanation.walkthrough: The child star's 1935 song puts the biscuits in her bowl; the idiom means in difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning in trouble, here taken literally from the song lyric.

clue.text: I'm caught in a'grip; cried Pen.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'I'm caught in a'grip; cried Pen. (8)': the letters of CRIED PEN rearrange to the answer, but no clue word signals the anagram (an old unindicated anagram), so the parse needs an indicator the clue lacks.
annotationWithheld.clue: I'm caught in a'grip; cried Pen.

clue.text: Made of teak no doubt.

parts.note: teak is a hardwood, so a boat built from it is in a sense a solid vessel; as one word it means adversity

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words the answer describes a tough-built boat; as one it means difficulty or suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe suffering or privation, punned here as a sturdy boat.

clue.text: Wine for the dance 7, That's the -stuff!"

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
sack is an old name for dry white wine from Spain or the Canaries

explanation.surface: A host offers wine for the dance and declares it just the thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' means cloth: a coarse woven fabric. The '7,' in the print is a stray mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse loosely woven fabric, originally made from sacking.

clue.text: Cold 'sources of sermons.

parts.note: As You Like It finds 'sermons in' rocks of this kind, which are proverbially cold

explanation.walkthrough: The Duke in As You Like It finds 'tongues in trees, books in the running brooks, sermons in' these.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces of rock, cold to touch and in Shakespeare a source of moral lessons.

clue.text: Butoh. the — sank like music on my-heart " (Coleridge).

definitions.text: Butoh. the — sank like music on my-heart

parts.words: Butoh. the — sank like music on my-heart
parts.note: in The Rime of the Ancient Mariner Coleridge writes that the absence of all sound 'sank like music on my heart'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Butoh.' is the print's run-together 'But oh'; the dash marks the missing word in the Coleridge quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: Total quiet, the absence of noise, which Coleridge likens to music.

clue.text: Redskins' victim could obviously an iron tonic

definitions.text: Redskins' victim could obviously an iron tonic

parts.words: Redskins' victim could obviously an iron tonic
parts.note: in old westerns the Native Americans' foe is the white settler, whose name for himself suggests a pallid, anaemic complexion that iron would cure

explanation.walkthrough: The print has lost a word such as 'use' before 'an iron tonic'. Iron tonics were taken for anaemia, whose sign is a pallid complexion.
explanation.definitionFit: A name for a white person attributed to Native Americans in westerns, literally one with a pallid complexion.

clue.text: Is all the fuss over fur or feather?

indicators.note: over here means the letters lie spread across the words that follow, a signal to find a run inside them

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the commotion is about a fur coat or a feathered hat.
explanation.definitionFit: An outburst of public excitement or uproar.

clue.text: Might be 15 or even 18.

parts.note: the numbers point to two other entries in the grid, an old East India merchantman and a teak-built boat, both kinds of ship

explanation.walkthrough: 15 is 15-across and 18 is 18-across; 'even' nods to the latter being a pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship or boat, of which an East India merchantman is one example.

clue.text: Gal is -involved in signs and abbreviations.'

indicators.note: involved means tangled or twisted, so the letters of the words before it are mixed up

explanation.surface: A girl gets caught up in sign language and shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a Latin word for the letters or symbols used as abbreviations in manuscripts and inscriptions.

clue.text: Her lover seemed herself to her.

definitions.text: Her lover seemed herself to her

parts.words: Her lover seemed herself to her
parts.note: Leander swam the Hellespont to his beloved priestess of Sestos; he seemed a champion in that woman's eyes, and that champion's word was also the priestess's name

explanation.walkthrough: The Greek legend of the priestess of Sestos and Leander, who drowned swimming to her.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion or idol, and also the priestess of Greek legend loved by Leander.

clue.text: G.O.C. to Saul.

parts.note: G.O.C. is General Officer Commanding; in the Bible the commander of King Saul's army was his cousin

explanation.walkthrough: G.O.C. is the British Army abbreviation for General Officer Commanding.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical captain of King Saul's army, described in modern military terms.

clue.text: What Saxifraga umbrosa displays?

parts.note: this saxifrage is known as London pride, so it displays self-esteem linked to a location

explanation.walkthrough: London pride is the common name of this saxifrage; the phrase means the most prominent position.
explanation.definitionFit: The most prominent or honoured position, read literally as the plant's civic pride.
